title: bug: JetBrains connect() re-syncs its bundled role docs and skills over newer ones the running daemon wrote, so an older plugin downgrades every seat's instructions on each reconnect
description:
Observed 2026-11-03 00:40Z (governor). The fleet's .moe/roles/worker.md matches docs/roles/worker.md at 03355c25, the 10-31 plugin build: a diff of 2 lines, the marker header. Against the live daemon's build 7262e53f, or the target tip, the diff is 8 lines. Its mtime is 2026-11-02 19:13Z, the daemon restart at the worktree switch. .moe/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md dates from 10-31 19:33Z, the plugin install. Seats in worktree mode therefore read pre-worktree docs, for example:
- worker.md still says "work in the project root by default (never a .worktrees/ checkout)";
- worker.reference.md lacks the "LANDING rule (worktree mode)" and Worktree mode sections that 03355c25..tip added.

Cause: both writers use the same rule, "overwrite when the on-disk marker sha differs":
- the daemon's writeInitFiles/writeSkillFiles, on every start (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts ~:694-700);
- the plugin's MoeProjectInitializer.syncRoleDocs/syncSkills (writeGeneratedDoc + shouldUpgradeGeneratedDoc, ~:163-196).
The plugin runs its sync on every connect(), in MoeProjectService.kt ~:150 via MoeDaemonSupervisor.ensureMoeInitialized ~:628, and in ensureDaemonRunningImpl ~:127. A sha difference is not an order, so the last writer wins. The plugin is rebuilt far less often than the daemon is swapped, so its bundled copy is usually the older one, and each reconnect downgrades the docs the newer daemon just wrote.

The planner decides the fix. Possible shapes:
- the plugin skips the doc sync when it attaches to a daemon it did not spawn, or whose /health version differs from its bundled one;
- the marker carries an orderable version, so neither writer ever downgrades.
Workaround until then: rebuild and reinstall the plugin from the current tip. It needs a PyCharm restart, which is the human's call. VS Code has no such sync; grep finds none in moe-vscode/src.
definitionOfDone: Connecting the JetBrains plugin to a running daemon never replaces a .moe/roles or .moe/skills file whose content came from a newer source than the plugin's bundled copy; a fresh project (no .moe/) and an unmarked user-customized file behave exactly as today.
JUnit tests in moe-jetbrains cover: plugin bundled copy older than on-disk daemon-written copy (kept), plugin copy newer (upgraded per the chosen rule), missing file (created), unmarked file (kept).
cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test passes (run under the gradle lease per the rails), with the exact command and counts in the completion evidence.

implementationPlan.description:
MoeProjectInitializer: add a create-only mode. Tests first.

The rule this task ships:
- On connect, the plugin only creates missing docs. A live daemon rewrote its own docs at its start, and they may be newer than this plugin's bundle.
- The plugin upgrades stale marked docs only right before it starts the daemon itself (step 2), because that daemon then serves the plugin's bundled docs.
- The fresh-.moe scaffold, unmarked files and non-markdown assets behave exactly as today.

(a) Tests first, in moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeProjectInitializerTest.kt. Use JUnit 4 and the file's tempDir() helper, and assertEquals on the full file text.
- I1 `create-only sync keeps a marked doc a newer daemon wrote` (DoD 2: older plugin copy kept). The target holds stampMarker("daemon v2 body"). writeGeneratedDoc(target, stampMarker("plugin v1 body"), upgrade = false) leaves it byte-identical.
- I2 `upgrade sync replaces an older marked doc` (DoD 2: newer plugin copy upgraded per the rule). The target holds stampMarker("v1"). writeGeneratedDoc(target, stampMarker("v2"), upgrade = true) leaves it equal to stampMarker("v2").
- I3 `both modes create a missing doc`. For upgrade in false and true, a missing target ends equal to the stamped text.
- I4 `both modes keep an unmarked doc`. Unmarked user text survives both modes byte-identical.
- I5 `create-only threads through role docs and every skill file`.
  - Pre-seed a roles/worker.md marked with a different sha. syncRoleDocs(moeDir, upgrade = false, bundled = mapOf("worker.md" to "plugin worker", "qa.md" to "plugin qa")) keeps it byte-identical and creates roles/qa.md = stampMarker("plugin qa").
  - syncSkills(moeDir, bundledDir, upgrade = false) keeps a stale-marked moe-planning/SKILL.md and a stale-marked manifest.json byte-identical, and creates a missing cpp/SKILL.md plus its nested templates/CMakeLists.txt.
  - Then rerun both with upgrade = true on the same tree. worker.md, SKILL.md and manifest.json now equal their bundled stamps, which proves the flag is the only difference.

(b) RED. Add the parameters, but IGNORE `upgrade` for now (today's behavior). Run under the lease: `--tests com.moe.util.MoeProjectInitializerTest`. I1 and I5 must FAIL; record their names.

(c) Implement.
- writeGeneratedDoc(target, stamped, upgrade: Boolean = true): create when missing. When the file exists, overwrite only if upgrade && shouldUpgradeGeneratedDoc(...).
- syncRoleDocs(moeDir, upgrade: Boolean = true, bundled: Map<String, String>? = null): use bundled ?: loadBundledRoleDocs().
- syncSkills(moeDir, bundledDir: File? = null, upgrade: Boolean = true): keep @JvmOverloads. Pass upgrade to the manifest.json/LICENSE writeGeneratedDoc and to syncSkillDir(source, targetDir, upgrade). Non-markdown assets stay create-only.
- Update the KDocs of writeGeneratedDoc, syncRoleDocs and syncSkills to say why upgrade=false exists.
- initializeProject and syncAgentContext keep the default upgrade = true, so a fresh scaffold and the explicit Init action are unchanged.

(d) GREEN. Rerun the same focused command; the whole class passes, existing tests unchanged.

Gradle: hold the `jetbrains-gradle` lease for every run and release it even on failure (mem:convention-jetbrains-gradle-lease). From the worktree root, use the step-4 command form with `test --tests com.moe.util.MoeProjectInitializerTest --rerun`, and leave the --tests value unquoted (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-gradle-from-wsl). Never pattern-kill a Gradle or Java process (GLOBAL rail 2). Write files with the Edit/Write tools only (GLOBAL rail 3).

GREEN: MoeProjectInitializerTest tests=22 failures=0 errors=0 (gradlew.bat test --tests com.moe.util.MoeProjectInitializerTest --rerun under the jetbrains-gradle lease). initializeProject/syncAgentContext unchanged (default upgrade=true).

implementationPlan.description:
MoeDaemonSupervisor: the connect path never upgrades. Only this plugin's own daemon start does. Tests first.

(a) Seam: add a new LAST constructor parameter `docSync: (File, Boolean) -> Unit = ::syncBundledDocs`.
- Put `syncBundledDocs(moeDir, upgrade)` in the companion object, beside ::defaultPortProbe.
- It calls MoeProjectInitializer.syncRoleDocs(moeDir, upgrade) and MoeProjectInitializer.syncSkills(moeDir, upgrade = upgrade), each in its own try/catch with a debug log, as ensureMoeInitialized does today. A role-doc failure must not skip the skills.
- Existing callers compile unchanged: MoeProjectService.kt:38 uses named args, and ManagedVmPanel.kt:116 passes two args.

(b) Tests first, in moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeDaemonSupervisorTest.kt.
- Give the private supervisor(...) helper a `docSync: (File, Boolean) -> Unit = { _, _ -> }` parameter, passed by name.
- Record into ONE events list: docSync adds "sync:$upgrade", and processStarter adds "start".
- Place the new tests next to the existing spawn tests (after `ensureDaemonRunning does not spawn when daemon is reachable` and after the cooldown test), not at the end of the class. task-fb0ab382 may also add tests to this file.
- S1 `connecting to an existing .moe only creates missing docs`: on an initializedRoot, ensureMoeInitialized() returns true and events == ["sync:false"].
- S2 `a reachable daemon never gets its docs upgraded` (DoD 1). Reuse the reachable fixture: daemon.json with pid 42 and port 9876, both probes true. Call ensureMoeInitialized() and then ensureDaemonRunning(), which is connect()'s order. events == ["sync:false", "sync:false"], with 0 starts.
- S3 `the upgrade runs once, right before this plugin starts its own daemon` (DoD 2: a newer plugin copy is upgraded when the plugin starts the daemon). On an initializedRoot with no daemon.json, ensureDaemonRunning() returns true and events == ["sync:false", "sync:true", "start"]. A second call inside the cooldown returns false and adds only "sync:false". End with killSpawnedDaemon().
- S4 `a refused spawn never upgrades docs`: after setSpawnAttempts(supervisor, 3), ensureDaemonRunning() is false and events == ["sync:false"].

(c) RED. First wire the seam like today: on an existing .moe, ensureMoeInitialized calls docSync(moeDir, true), and the spawn path calls nothing. Run `--tests com.moe.services.MoeDaemonSupervisorTest` under the lease. S1 to S4 must FAIL; record their names.

(d) Implement.
- ensureMoeInitialized(): leave the missing-.moe branch (initializeProject) unchanged. For an existing .moe, call docSync(moeDir, false). Replace the 'Always sync role docs and skills…' comment with the reason: a live daemon rewrote these at its own start and may be newer than this plugin's bundle. Stale copies are upgraded by the daemon at every start, or by the spawn path when this plugin starts the daemon itself.
- ensureDaemonRunningImpl(): call docSync(File(projectBasePath, ".moe"), true) exactly once. Place it after `val direct = …`, so the reachable and other-side returns, the cooldown and max-attempt gates, and a protected refusal all skip it. Place it before the `try { val pb = …` that launches the process. Add a one-line comment: this plugin is about to start its own daemon, which serves the plugin's bundled docs.
- Error handling: a docSync exception logs at debug and never blocks connect or spawn, as today.

(e) GREEN. Rerun the same focused command; the whole class passes.

Use the same lease and command form as step 1.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of the whole diff, then complete_task.
(a) DoD 1: no connect path can overwrite an existing file. ensureMoeInitialized passes upgrade=false. The only upgrade=true call in the supervisor sits after every early return and immediately before the launch. grep the diff for docSync and syncRoleDocs/syncSkills calls and list each call with its flag.
(b) The fresh-.moe branch (initializeProject) is unchanged. Unmarked files are still never overwritten in either mode. Non-markdown skill assets are still create-only. InitMoeAction and MoeToolWindowPanel still call initializeProject with today's semantics.

(d) Concurrency: the upgrade sync runs only inside the spawn path, which is already serialized by the cooldown, the attempt counter and the protected replacementInFlight guard. Two reconnects cannot both upgrade without both spawning.
(e) Residual window, to state in the completion summary rather than fix here. A daemon in mid-restart looks unreachable, so the plugin may run its upgrade sync just before its own spawn attempt. That is the pre-existing spawn race, now the only remaining downgrade path. The restarted daemon rewrites its own docs at its start.
(f) Tests are mutation-resistant: assertEquals on full text and on the full events list. RED was recorded in steps 1 and 2.

A live daemon rewrote those at its own start, and they may be newer than the plugin's bundled copy. On connect the plugin only creates missing files. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- An orderable marker (version or timestamp in the stamp) was rejected. It changes the stamp format on both writers, regenerates initFiles.ts and the 1.4 MB skillFiles.ts, needs history at build time (CI checks out shallow), and breaks the 'plugin and daemon stamp byte-identically' invariant. Far over one task's size.
- Ordering from shipped-sha history was rejected. Role docs have SHIPPED_ROLE_BODY_SHAS only inside the daemon's generated JS, and skills have no history list at all, so the plugin would need a new generated manifest across packages.
- Comparing /health versions was rejected. Dev builds share one SemVer, so equal versions with different docs would still downgrade.
- Never upgrading at all (pure create-only) was rejected. It drops DoD 2's 'plugin copy newer: upgraded' case.
- Chosen: the task description's first shape. Docs follow the daemon that serves the project. The plugin upgrades only when it is the one starting the daemon, and is create-only on connect.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- connect() calls ensureMoeInitialized() before it knows whether a daemon is live, and ensureDaemonRunningImpl() calls it again first thing. The old unconditional sync therefore ran on every reconnect, including right after a newer daemon restarted, which is the observed 19:13Z downgrade.
- The daemon rewrites its own bundled docs on every start, so the plugin's upgrade only matters on its own spawn path, where the daemon it launches ships the same docs.
- The supervisor already injects every effect through constructor lambdas with companion defaults; docSync follows that.
- Unit tests have no plugin bundle (PluginManagerCore finds nothing), so supervisor tests must use the seam. A real-file assertion through the supervisor would pass vacuously.
planningNotes.risks:
1. Residual window: a daemon in mid-restart looks unreachable, so the plugin may run its upgrade sync just before its own (pre-existing, racy) spawn attempt. It is narrower than today's every-connect downgrade. Name it in the completion summary.
2. MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND pointing at another daemon: the plugin upgrades its bundled docs before the launch, and that daemon then rewrites its own at its start. The result is transiently mixed and then correct.
3. task-fb0ab382 (PLANNING) and task-7faede18 (PLANNING) may also touch MoeDaemonSupervisorTest.kt or MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt. Insert tests beside related ones rather than at the class end, to keep the landing hunks apart.
4. WT-18 (task-1b2e6fe3, WORKING) edits CLAUDE.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. Keep this task's doc hunks to the named lines.
5. Gradle: always hold the jetbrains-gradle lease, use --rerun, and never pattern-kill java or gradle processes.

- If MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND points at a different daemon build, the plugin upgrades and then that daemon rewrites at its start: briefly mixed, then correct.
No daemon, proxy or VS Code files changed.
